final_candidate.hypothesis: At fixed framework geometry (lsd_p fixed), adsorbates whose heavy-atom enclosing radius (SPAN) is large relative to the included-along-free-path sphere diameter (lsd_p) experience tighter rotational confinement and therefore a larger entropy loss over R = (Sgas - Sads)/R; equivalently, entropy loss decreases as the descriptor exp(-q_SPAN/q_lsd_p) increases toward its mobility-like bound of 1. This is a conditional transfer of the reported FER/FAU cavity-confinement trend (E02) and the MCM-22 radius-of-gyration-vs-available-space argument (E06) to this dataset, mediated by available proxies.
final_candidate.rationale: Mechanism: rotational (with possible translational coupling) degrees of freedom are progressively suppressed as molecular size approaches the confining pore dimension. The descriptor maps this via two proxies with explicit limitations: (1) SPAN is a heavy-atom/implicit-H enclosing radius, not the radius of gyration including hydrogens, and is a legitimate physical 0 for the 54 single-site entries (where the descriptor saturates at exp(0)=1, i.e., no size-based rotational confinement proxy); (2) lsd_p (Zeo++ Dif) is the largest included sphere along the free-sphere path, NOT the bottleneck Df and NOT necessarily the global cavity diameter Di of the FER/FAU comparison; using it as a cavity-size proxy assumes the adsorption site lies along the accessible free path. The exponential form is an empirical bounded mapping chosen so the descriptor stays in (0,1] on finite support and monotonically saturates; it is not derived from a partition function, and no source coefficient is reused.
final_candidate.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, holding lsd_p fixed at training quantile values, predicted entropy loss over R does not increase with SPAN over its training range [0, 6.24082991], or if the apparent SPAN dependence is fully absorbed by lsd_p alone (framework-only confinement explanation), or if performance requires treating the SPAN=0 single-site branch differently (indicating the implicit-H heavy-atom radius is not the operative size proxy). A competing explanation is that any correlation arises from SPAN co-varying with adsorbate mass/VMW rather than confinement; this is not excluded by the descriptor itself.
final_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Assumes (a) heavy-atom SPAN is an adequate stand-in for the molecular radius governing rotational confinement; (b) lsd_p is an adequate stand-in for the local cavity dimension controlling rotational freedom at the adsorption site, acknowledging the documented distinction Dif != Df != Di; (c) the reported cavity-size/rotational-entropy-loss relation from zeolite comparisons transfers to this framework/adsorbate set; (d) the exponential saturation is an empirical choice, not a physical law; (e) zero SPAN values are physical (single-site) and preserved, with the descriptor taking its maximum mobility-like value there rather than being imputed.
final_candidate.boundary_behavior: Finite training support: SPAN in [0, 6.24082991] (with 54 legitimate zeros) and lsd_p in [3.3452, 15.5604] (strictly positive), so q_SPAN/q_lsd_p >= 0 is finite and the descriptor lies in (0, 1]. Physical zeros of SPAN are preserved: single-site adsorbates give descriptor 1 (no heavy-atom size confinement proxy) rather than an imputed value; they may still lose translational entropy not captured here.

However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. draft.rationale: Mechanism: rotational (with possible translational coupling) degrees of freedom are progressively suppressed as molecular size approaches the confining pore dimension. descriptor_candidate.name: bottleneck_passing_mobility
descriptor_candidate.hypothesis: At fixed framework bottleneck geometry (lsd_f fixed), adsorbates whose largest heavy-atom pair distance (GeDi) is large relative to the largest passing free sphere (lsd_f) must thread through narrow constrictions that are tight compared to their molecular extent, and therefore experience a larger loss of translational (and coupled hindered reorientational) freedom over R = (Sgas - Sads)/R; equivalently, entropy loss decreases as the descriptor exp(-q_GeDi/q_lsd_f) increases toward its unconstrained mobility-like bound of 1. This transfers the reported confinement trend of E02 (smaller pore, larger entropy loss) and the MFI/FAU comparison of E01/E04 from average cavity diameter to the passing-bottleneck quantity actually available in this dataset, treating lsd_f as the operative geometric constraint for motion through the framework rather than a global cavity diameter.
descriptor_candidate.rationale: lsd_f is the Zeo++ Df bottleneck (largest sphere able to pass through a periodic free path), not the global cavity diameter Di, and lsd_p (used in the round-1 descriptor) is the included-along-path sphere, not the passing bottleneck; using lsd_f here targets a physically distinct geometric constraint from the round-1 descriptor exp(-q_SPAN/q_lsd_p), which used the included-sphere scale. GeDi is a heavy-atom largest-pair distance in the implicit-H representation and ignores hydrogen extents, so very small true clearances may be misjudged for hydrogen-rich molecules; q_GeDi/q_lsd_f is a dimensionless ratio of training-referenced quantities and its value 1 does not correspond to a physical equality of GeDi and lsd_f. GeDi = 0 for the 54 single-site training entries is a legitimate zero that maps to descriptor value exp(0) = 1 (unconstrained point-particle mobility bound), not an imputation. The mechanism (translational hindrance at constrictions) is an empirical extension of reported cage-size trends to bottleneck geometry and is not established for this dataset; AV is deliberately not used because it is a mass-specific fixed-probe accessibility and cannot support a molecule-specific free-volume claim.
descriptor_candidate.falsification_criteria: If predictive performance attributable to this descriptor disappears or reverses when lsd_p (included-along-path scale) is held fixed instead of lsd_f, the effect is better explained by cavity-scale confinement (already captured by the round-1 descriptor) rather than bottleneck-controlled translational hindrance. Likewise, if the descriptor's association is driven only by adsorbate size (GeDi alone) with no residual dependence on lsd_f, the proposed framework-side mechanism is falsified in favor of a pure adsorbate-size explanation.

appended.name: exp_neg_span_over_included_pore_q
appended.hypothesis: At fixed framework geometry (lsd_p fixed), adsorbates whose heavy-atom enclosing radius (SPAN) is large relative to the included-along-free-path sphere diameter (lsd_p) experience tighter rotational confinement and therefore a larger entropy loss over R = (Sgas - Sads)/R; equivalently, entropy loss decreases as the descriptor exp(-q_SPAN/q_lsd_p) increases toward its mobility-like bound of 1. This is a conditional transfer of the reported FER/FAU cavity-confinement trend (E02) and the MCM-22 radius-of-gyration-vs-available-space argument (E06) to this dataset, mediated by available proxies.
appended.rationale: Mechanism: rotational (with possible translational coupling) degrees of freedom are progressively suppressed as molecular size approaches the confining pore dimension. The descriptor maps this via two proxies with explicit limitations: (1) SPAN is a heavy-atom/implicit-H enclosing radius, not the radius of gyration including hydrogens, and is a legitimate physical 0 for the 54 single-site entries (where the descriptor saturates at exp(0)=1, i.e., no size-based rotational confinement proxy); (2) lsd_p (Zeo++ Dif) is the largest included sphere along the free-sphere path, NOT the bottleneck Df and NOT necessarily the global cavity diameter Di of the FER/FAU comparison; using it as a cavity-size proxy assumes the adsorption site lies along the accessible free path. The exponential form is an empirical bounded mapping chosen so the descriptor stays in (0,1] on finite support and monotonically saturates; it is not derived from a partition function, and no source coefficient is reused.
appended.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, holding lsd_p fixed at training quantile values, predicted entropy loss over R does not increase with SPAN over its training range [0, 6.24082991], or if the apparent SPAN dependence is fully absorbed by lsd_p alone (framework-only confinement explanation), or if performance requires treating the SPAN=0 single-site branch differently (indicating the implicit-H heavy-atom radius is not the operative size proxy). A competing explanation is that any correlation arises from SPAN co-varying with adsorbate mass/VMW rather than confinement; this is not excluded by the descriptor itself.
appended.proxy_assumptions: Assumes (a) heavy-atom SPAN is an adequate stand-in for the molecular radius governing rotational confinement; (b) lsd_p is an adequate stand-in for the local cavity dimension controlling rotational freedom at the adsorption site, acknowledging the documented distinction Dif != Df != Di; (c) the reported cavity-size/rotational-entropy-loss relation from zeolite comparisons transfers to this framework/adsorbate set; (d) the exponential saturation is an empirical choice, not a physical law; (e) zero SPAN values are physical (single-site) and preserved, with the descriptor taking its maximum mobility-like value there rather than being imputed.
appended.boundary_behavior: Finite training support: SPAN in [0, 6.24082991] (with 54 legitimate zeros) and lsd_p in [3.3452, 15.5604] (strictly positive), so q_SPAN/q_lsd_p >= 0 is finite and the descriptor lies in (0, 1]. Physical zeros of SPAN are preserved: single-site adsorbates give descriptor 1 (no heavy-atom size confinement proxy) rather than an imputed value; they may still lose translational entropy not captured here.
